description.value: This longitudinal voxel-based morphometry study investigated local and global brain-volume changes in alcoholic patients during the first 3 months following alcohol detoxification, compared with healthy controls and examined separately by gender.

spans.text: With this longitudinal study, we aimed to investigate local changes in brain volumes in the first 3 months following alcohol detoxification using voxel-based morphometry (VBM), which provides the opportunity of a fully automatic analysis of the anatomy of the whole brain and to specify volume loss in regional cerebral matter.

description.value: Longitudinal observational study of alcoholic patients and healthy controls, with MRI examinations shortly after detoxification and again 3 months later in a subset.

value: VBM analysis yielded several brain areas with significant GM volume losses in the whole patient group compared with controls, most prominently in the insula, followed by the middle and anterior cingulate gyri, parahippocampal gyrus, amygdala, and superior temporal gyrus.
The findings corroborate widespread cerebral volume loss in recently detoxified alcoholics, with loss localized particularly to the insula and cingulate gyrus.
